note: Same checkpoint as b04, and deliberately the same file rather than a copy: b04's model.json carries the full candidate comparison, the QM reference protocol and the per-atom charge measurements, and duplicating them here would let the two drift. Read ../b04_sn2_chloride/model.json for the basis; this file records only what is specific to b05.
why_no_factory_of_its_own: The factory exists because prrs.calculators.mace_factory does not pass model_type and would load PolarMACE as a plain MACE -- computing the wrong thing WITHOUT RAISING. That is a property of the checkpoint class, not of the grid, so b05 reaches the same function through the same --calculator hook instead of growing a second copy of it.
why_this_one_for_b05: Default from P4 onward (user, 2026-09-04), and the ionic half of the two-reaction comparison that decided it was measured on exactly this kind of system: charge -1, a leaving halide, a heavy-atom reaction coordinate.

unverified_for_this_grid.hydroxide: POLAR-1's ionic validation is one number on ONE anion: Cl- + CH3Cl, central barrier +2.09 kcal/mol against wB97M-V/def2-TZVPD. NOTHING here establishes it on hydroxide, on a C-H abstraction, or on an alkene product. Preflight measures that the model responds to charge on this structure; that is a sanity check, not accuracy. Any energetic statement from this grid inherits this line.
unverified_for_this_grid.training_set: UNVERIFIED -- not readable from the checkpoint. Unchanged from b04: this is the open question about POLAR-1's provenance, and it is a reason criteria may not rest on its energetics.
unverified_for_this_grid.three_fragment_products: The elimination channel's product set has THREE fragments (alkene + water + halide). No model in this project has been checked on a three-fragment dissociated state, and a charge-aware model has an obvious way to be wrong there: the -1 has to end up on the chloride rather than smeared across the set. Preflight gate 8 measures where the charge goes.
